A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Agent-System Interface work. Their main text, figures, tables, mathematical material, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v2 reports original mapper-performance experiments on nine benchmarks, code-generation tests, and feedback ablations in Section 5, with additional results and generated-code examples in the appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds performance-distribution summaries and failure statistics in Section 5.1 and Appendix A.4.

M1.justification: The DSL/compiler, modular mapper agent, generative optimization, and keyword-based AutoGuide mechanism remain unchanged. Expanded descriptions and the shortened Figure A7 mapper example do not establish a change to the optimization procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Circuit, Stencil, Pennant, and the same six matrix-multiplication benchmarks. The ten mapping-strategy code-generation tests and three-benchmark feedback ablation also remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same expert, random, OPRO, OpenTuner, C++, and feedback-configuration comparators. Although v2's detailed lines-of-code table is removed, the aggregate DSL-versus-C++ comparison remains.

E3.justification: Hardware, GPT-4o version, iteration budgets, throughput normalization, and ablation procedures are retained. v3 explicitly specifies zero throughput for invalid mappers, but does not report a revision to the existing evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Section 5.1 adds an error breakdown showing that 74 of 90 random mappers fail at runtime. Appendix A.4 adds analysis of unsuccessful optimization runs and invalid configurations. The existing DSL and AutoGuide ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: v3 Appendix A.4 adds explicit standard deviations and worst, median, and best throughput summaries for Trace and OpenTuner. Both versions already report five-run evaluations and averaged trajectories; this expands statistical reporting without establishing additional runs.

E6.justification: v3 adds numerical distribution summaries and the 74/90 random-mapper failure count, while removing v2 Table A1's per-application code-size results. Section 5.2 corrects three resolved C++ compilation errors to four, matching the unchanged Table 2. The performance curves and headline speedups remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 newly supplies a formal DSL grammar defining statement and expression productions. This is a limited formal specification addition; the online-optimization formulation and assumptions in Section 4.2 remain unchanged, with no new proofs or guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and performance claims: DSL plus AutoGuide, up to 1.34× over expert mappers, 3.8× over OpenTuner with the stated iteration budgets, and tuning reduced from days to minutes.

C2.justification: v3 explains best-run selection through offline optimization and reuse under fixed application, input, and hardware conditions. It also qualifies DSL expressiveness and connects optimization failures to invalid configurations, runtime correctness checks, and mitigation through repeated searches.

D1.justification: v3 adds a DSL syntax specification, explicitly documents zero-throughput handling of invalid mappers, and revises the generated Solomonik mapper listing in Figure A7. These are documentation changes; hardware and software disclosures otherwise remain stable.

R1.justification: Section 5.1 adds citations to Yadav et al. (2022), Jangda et al. (2022), and Zheng et al. (2025) to motivate matrix-multiplication benchmarks and their relevance. The related-work discussion and central novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 expands selected method and evaluation paragraphs, introduces grammar and statistics appendix subsections, and updates the title to plural 'Interfaces' and publication information. The overall narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v3 enlarges and repositions existing figures, removes the code-size table, and adds a grammar display and two statistics tables. Figure A7 is shortened so both Solomonik examples share a page. The main diagrams and plotted data are retained.

improvement.justification: The new variability summaries and failure explanations make optimization reliability easier to assess beyond the retained average and best-performance plots. This provides a limited transparency improvement, partly offset by removing the per-application code-size evidence supporting the retained 14× reduction claim. The core method and experimental coverage remain stable.
